 Polish president turns back from Senegal trip as top court chief suspended
 Reuters 
 31 October, 2026 12:00 am IST 
 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin 
 (c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026 
 Follow Us : 
 Text Size:
 A- 
 A+

 WARSAW, Oct 30 (Reuters) – Polish President Karol Nawrocki turned back his plane en route to Senegal on Friday after police entered the premises of Poland’s top court and its president was suspended.
 “At a moment like this, the President must be in Poland. I am cutting short my flight to Senegal. I am returning,” he said on X.
 Police said officers entered the premises of the Constitutional Tribunal after incidents outside the court, including the throwing of dangerous objects at police.
 Show Full Article
 The tribunal said on its website that the court’s president, Bogdan Swieczkowski, had been suspended on Friday.
 A long-running political dispute over the Constitutional Tribunal has effectively paralysed the institution.
 Earlier this year, Nawrocki, an ally of Poland’s former nationalist government, refused to swear in three of six judges nominated by parliament, while Swieczkowski declined to allow judges elected by the current parliamentary majority to assume their duties.
 (Reporting by Marek StrzeleckiEditing by Ros Russell)
